description: The module's single sign-on wiring: its Authentik application/provider and the groups allowed to use it.
_note: update-service.sh execs install-service.sh, which is fully reconcile-in-place (ADR-006 Phase 4, #56): it refreshes the OIDC app/provider, re-applies the access bindings and rewrites the VM secrets env, and is safe on every update cycle. There is no per-field drift loop to extract.

identity.description: OIDC integration contract for a module that dependsOn identity:identity (ADR-006). Consumed by services/identity/install-service.sh. Omit for forward-auth modules (those use identity:accessControl).

providesAdminRole.description: Opt-in: create and bind a <scope>-<module>-admins group so a per-module admin role exists. Default false keeps Authentik uncluttered for modules with no admin concept.

oidcRedirectPaths.description: OIDC callback paths, each appended to https://<proxyDomain> to form a redirect URI. Default suits Nextcloud user_oidc.

scopes.description: OIDC scope-mapping names the provider should expose. Default (empty) yields openid/email/profile; Authentik’s profile scope already emits the groups claim.

secretsEnv.description: Absolute path on the module VM where OIDC_CLIENT_ID/OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET/OIDC_DISCOVERY_URI are written (mode 600). Default /etc/secrets/<base-module>.env.

configureService.description: systemd unit on the module VM to restart after writing the env so the app registers the provider (e.g. nextcloud-configure-oidc.service). Empty defaults to <base>-configure-oidc.service (best-effort restart; warns if absent). Set to "none" for modules that register the provider themselves via the app's API (e.g. Portainer on Debian) — no unit is restarted.

identity.changeNote: The whole SSO block — provider type, redirect URIs, the groups bound to the application. Re-applying it updates Authentik; sessions already issued keep working, so there is no downtime to authorize.
